No other lesions were identified. The patient was readmitted, and a repeat lumbar puncture was performed. CSF analysis now showed a WBC count of 210 cells/μL with 94% lymphocytes, protein of 98.6 mg/dL, and glucose of 38 mg/dL. CSF cytology revealed atypical large lymphoid cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios. Flow cytometry of the CSF demonstrated a monoclonal B-cell population expressing CD19, CD20, and CD22 with loss of CD5 and CD10. A stereotactic brain biopsy was performed under general anesthesia. Histopathological examination revealed a diffuse infiltration of atypical large lymphoid cells with centroblastic morphology. Immunohistochemistry confirmed positivity for CD20, PAX5, and MUM1, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. The cells were negative for CD3, CD5, and CD10. The final diagnosis was primary central nervous system diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PCNS-DLBCL). The interventional team elected to proceed with a second 20-mg alteplase dose at 18:15, having observed no new haemorrhagic complication beyond the already-managed arterial access-site oozing. A repeat coagulation panel at 18:40 showed platelets of 58 × 109/L, fibrinogen of 1.12 g/L, and aPTT of 52.3 s. The falling fibrinogen was interpreted as consumption secondary to ongoing thrombolysis rather than a consumptive coagulopathy, given the absence of a rising D-dimer disproportionate to the expected lytic effect and the stable haemoglobin. Neurological examination again revealed marked nuchal rigidity without focal deficits; fundoscopy was initially reported as normal.
